newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy will meet EMU deficit-GDP goal.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy will meet EMU deficit-GDP goal.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday that Italy would meet the Maastricht goal of a three-percent deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio in time for the planned start of European economic and monetary union in 1999.
"We will meet the ratio between deficit and GDP in the terms laid down by Maastricht," Prodi told question time in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).

Prodi said Italy had already met the Maastricht Treaty targets on interest rates, exchange rates and inflation and was well on the way to meeting the deficit-GDP goal in time for the planned single currency launch.

"Italy is moving towards the parameters even concerning debt," Prodi said, referring to the fifth Maastricht goal that wants countries to move towards a 60 percent ratio of total debt to GDP. Italy's ratio is currently more than 120 percent.

"We are already in order on three points. The fourth we will meet, and progress on the fifth is exactly in line with other European countries," he said, noting that only Luxembourg currently made the grade on the total deficit criterion.

Prodi said Italy's partners considered its strategy "the most vigorous and most appropriate" for EMU entry. Prodi has pinned his survival to EMU entry, despite German fears that Italian founding membership could weaken the new euro.
